newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Stg/mark vols up in Europe on spot slump.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Stg/mark vols up in Europe on spot slump.

text.p: Sterling/mark option volatilities were higher in morning Europe on spot's continued weakness following Monday's sharp plunge.
Spot sterling steadied below 3.00 marks in morning Europe after dropping over five pfennigs Monday and overnight amid concerns that UK interest rates may not be increased as soon as expected.
Option dealers said volatilities were marked higher as players scrambled for cover but activity so far has been confined to short-covering in short-dated, at-the-money options.

"People have been long all the way up so we've some of those positions being unwound," said a U.S. bank options dealer. "But things have calmed down, the market seems to have reached a point where it thinks we're going into a period of consolidation."

One-month sterling/mark option volatility edged up to 11.2/11.7 percent against 10.9/11.4 percent late Monday in Europe. However, one-year volatility remained stable at 9.60/9.95 percent from 9.5/9.9.
The sterling/mark risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility in calls relative to puts, leaned towards a bias for pound puts at 0.0/0.5 pct from its long-running bias of calls.
Dealers said the picture was much the same for cable as the spot rate made a similar downmove, but the bulk of options repositioning was seen Monday and option vols today were steadier.
One-month cable vols stood at 9.6/9.9 percent against 9.7/10.2 percent Monday, though up from levels below 9.0 percent late last week.
The sterling/dollar risk reversal was steady at 0.3/0.8 percent for sterling puts.
Dollar/yen option volatilities were steady to slightly firmer with one-month vols finding support from spot's extended gain above the key 117 yen level.
The dollar/yen risk reversal extended Monday's switch to a bias for yen puts after long-favouring a strong leaning to yen calls.
But dealers said talk of option barriers in the 118 region were being defended and could put a brake on further dollar gains.

"The dollar/yen downside risk is not over yet despite the collapse in the risk reversal," said a UK bank dealer. "A break above 118 to 120 will likely see the Japanese authorities talking the yen back up again, raising the risk of an overshoot lower."

One-month dollar/yen volatility was trading at 10.8/11.3 percent from 10.9/11.2 percent late Monday. One-year dollar/yen vol was little changed at 11.4/11.9 though dealers cited ongoing demand at this end of the market.
Dollar/mark volatility was slightly easier on spot's failure to hold above the 1.84 marks level but activity was relatively muted.
One-month volatility was trading at 10.1/10.5 percent from 10.4/10.7 late Monday. The risk reversal was unchanged and continued to favour mark puts at 0.6/0.9.
